questions.question: Differentiate descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics.
questions.preferred_answer: Descriptive analytics explains what happened, diagnostic analytics investigates why it happened, predictive analytics estimates what may happen, and prescriptive analytics recommends actions under stated objectives and constraints. A strong answer also notes that the categories can overlap within one decision workflow.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How do you convert a vague request such as 'improve customer retention' into an analytical problem?
questions.preferred_answer: Clarify the decision to be made, target population, time horizon, definition of retention, controllable levers, constraints, and success metric. Translate the request into testable questions, identify required data, record assumptions, and agree on what action will follow each possible result.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the unit of analysis, and why must it be defined before querying data?
questions.preferred_answer: The unit of analysis is the entity represented by one analytical observation, such as one customer, order, session, or customer-month. Defining it prevents accidental duplication, invalid averages, and mismatched joins because every metric and feature must be interpreted at a known grain.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the difference between a population and a sample?
questions.preferred_answer: A population is the complete set about which a conclusion is intended; a sample is the observed subset used for analysis. The sample should be selected and evaluated so that sampling error and selection bias are understood before generalising results.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Differentiate a dimension from a measure in BI.
questions.preferred_answer: Dimensions describe and group observations, such as date, region, customer, or product. Measures are quantitative values aggregated in context, such as revenue, quantity, margin, or distinct customers. A field can behave differently depending on the model and analytical question.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the difference between leading and lagging indicators?
questions.preferred_answer: A lagging indicator records an outcome after it occurs, such as monthly churn. A leading indicator is an earlier signal associated with that outcome, such as declining usage. Leading indicators are useful only when their relationship, timing, and actionability are validated.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why does correlation not establish causation?
questions.preferred_answer: Correlation can arise from confounding, reverse causality, selection effects, common trends, or chance. Causal claims require a credible identification strategy such as randomisation or a justified quasi-experimental design, plus assumptions and sensitivity checks.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is a baseline, and how would you choose one?
questions.preferred_answer: A baseline is the reference against which change is assessed. Choose it to match the decision and seasonality: a prior comparable period, control group, forecast, target, or established benchmark. Document any differences that make the comparison imperfect.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why should an analyst examine segments instead of only overall averages?
questions.preferred_answer: Overall averages can hide materially different behaviours and even reverse within subgroups. Segment by decision-relevant dimensions, confirm adequate sample sizes, avoid uncontrolled slicing, and distinguish exploratory findings from pre-specified comparisons.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How would you define and analyse a conversion funnel?
questions.preferred_answer: Define ordered, observable events, eligibility rules, identity logic, time windows, and mutually consistent denominators. Calculate stage conversion and drop-off, segment results, inspect latency between stages, and validate event completeness before recommending interventions.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is cohort analysis, and when is it preferable to a calendar-period trend?
questions.preferred_answer: Cohort analysis groups entities by a shared starting event or attribute, such as acquisition month, and follows them over comparable elapsed time. It separates lifecycle effects from changes in the mix of newly added users.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What makes a useful north-star metric?
questions.preferred_answer: It should reflect recurring customer value, connect to sustainable business outcomes, be understandable and measurable, and respond to meaningful product changes. It needs guardrail metrics so teams cannot improve it by damaging quality, trust, cost, or another stakeholder outcome.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How should assumptions and analytical limitations be communicated?
questions.preferred_answer: State the assumption, why it was necessary, evidence supporting it, likely direction and magnitude of risk, tests performed, and what would change the conclusion. Separate known facts, estimates, and unresolved uncertainty rather than hiding caveats in footnotes.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How would you choose a decision threshold for an analytical score?
questions.preferred_answer: Evaluate the costs and benefits of false positives, false negatives, review capacity, prevalence, fairness, and operational constraints. Compare candidate thresholds on an appropriate validation set and document the trade-off rather than choosing a threshold solely for a statistical metric.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What makes an analysis reproducible?
questions.preferred_answer: Versioned code or queries, fixed source references, documented transformations, controlled parameters, preserved environments where relevant, deterministic steps or recorded random seeds, data-quality checks, and a clear path from source to output.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What should a decision-ready analytical recommendation contain?
questions.preferred_answer: Lead with the decision and expected impact, then present the evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, assumptions, implementation owner, measurable next step, and monitoring plan. The recommendation should be proportional to the strength of the evidence.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How do you identify the right stakeholders for an analytics initiative?
questions.preferred_answer: Map decision owners, data owners, subject-matter experts, producers, consumers, affected operational teams, and governance or privacy roles. Clarify who approves definitions, who acts on the result, and whose incentives or risks may be overlooked.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: Differentiate business, stakeholder, solution, and data requirements.
questions.preferred_answer: Business requirements describe desired outcomes; stakeholder requirements describe stakeholder needs; solution requirements describe capabilities and qualities; data requirements define needed entities, fields, grain, history, quality, access, and lineage. Trace them so technical work remains connected to the decision.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: What is the difference between a metric and a KPI?
questions.preferred_answer: A metric is any quantitative measure. A KPI is a deliberately selected metric tied to a strategic or operational objective, with an owner, target, time horizon, interpretation, and action. Every KPI is a metric, but not every metric deserves KPI status.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: What fields belong in a formal metric definition?
questions.preferred_answer: Include business meaning, formula, numerator and denominator, grain, population, filters, exclusions, time basis, currency or units, source, refresh cadence, owner, quality rules, target, and examples. Also state how changes are governed and versioned.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: What is a vanity metric, and how would you challenge one?
questions.preferred_answer: A vanity metric looks favourable but does not reliably guide a decision or connect to value, such as raw registrations without activation or retention. Ask what action it changes, what denominator or comparison is missing, and whether it can improve while the real outcome worsens.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How do OKRs and KPIs relate?
questions.preferred_answer: An objective states a qualitative direction; key results define measurable outcomes for that objective. KPIs monitor ongoing health or performance. A KPI may be used as a key result, but operational KPIs often continue beyond one OKR cycle.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How would you write acceptance criteria for a dashboard?
questions.preferred_answer: Specify intended users and decisions, metric definitions, filters, default state, refresh and latency, row-level access, visual behaviour, export needs, performance, accessibility, reconciliation tolerance, and sign-off evidence. Use examples for ambiguous interactions.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: A stakeholder keeps adding dashboard requests. How do you control scope without blocking value?
questions.preferred_answer: Return to the decision and priority outcomes, classify requests as essential, deferred, or exploratory, estimate impact, expose trade-offs, and agree on a minimum useful release. Record a backlog and change-control path rather than silently absorbing work.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: Sales and Finance define revenue differently. What should the analyst do?
questions.preferred_answer: Do not average or choose privately. Document both definitions, purposes, source systems, timing, adjustments, and owners; reconcile to authoritative records; facilitate a governed definition or clearly labelled variants; and prevent ambiguous reuse in shared reports.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How can service-level concepts be applied to an analytics product?
questions.preferred_answer: Define measurable expectations such as refresh completion, freshness, availability, query response, defect response, or data-quality thresholds. An internal SLO is a target used to operate the product; an SLA is a formal commitment with specified consequences or governance.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: Why is requirements traceability useful in BI delivery?
questions.preferred_answer: It connects business outcomes and stakeholder needs to data elements, transformations, tests, visuals, and acceptance evidence. Traceability helps assess change impact, identify uncovered requirements, explain outputs, and retire unused work.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How would you prioritise analytics requirements?
questions.preferred_answer: Compare decision value, urgency, risk reduction, regulatory need, user reach, effort, dependencies, data readiness, and reversibility. Use an agreed method, but preserve judgement and explicitly identify mandatory work and uncertainty.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: Write the essential structure of an analytics user story.
questions.preferred_answer: State the user or role, the decision or task, the required insight or capability, and the value. Add testable acceptance criteria covering data, definitions, filters, security, refresh, performance, and expected examples; the story format alone is not a complete requirement.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How would you measure whether a dashboard is successful?
questions.preferred_answer: Combine usage with outcome evidence: active intended users, repeat use, task completion, time saved, decision cycle, reduction in manual work, data trust, support burden, and business effects. Avoid treating page views as proof of decision impact.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: What questions would you ask in a stakeholder requirements interview?
questions.preferred_answer: Ask what decision is being made, current process, users, frequency, consequences of error or delay, definitions, examples, exceptions, comparisons, required detail, action thresholds, data constraints, access rules, and how success will be verified.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Business Requirements, Metrics, KPIs, and Stakeholders
questions.question: How should the same analysis be adapted for an executive and an operational analyst?
questions.preferred_answer: Keep the underlying facts consistent but tailor depth and action. Executives need the decision, impact, risk, and options; operational analysts need definitions, segments, exceptions, workflow details, and drill paths. Both need visible uncertainty and provenance.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: Name important data-quality dimensions and explain why a single quality score can mislead.
questions.preferred_answer: Common dimensions include accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness, and fitness for purpose. A composite score can hide a critical failure in one dimension and depends on arbitrary weighting, so report dimensions and business impact separately.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What checks belong in an initial data profile?
questions.preferred_answer: Inspect row counts, schema and types, nulls, distinctness, ranges, quantiles, categorical frequencies, patterns, duplicate keys, referential integrity, date coverage, outliers, and changes by partition or source. Compare findings with expected business rules.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: How do you decide what to do with missing values?
questions.preferred_answer: First determine meaning and mechanism: truly absent, not applicable, not collected, suppressed, delayed, or extraction failure. Measure patterns and business impact, then choose deletion, explicit category, imputation, model handling, or remediation. Preserve a missingness indicator when informative.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: How do exact duplicates differ from business duplicates?
questions.preferred_answer: Exact duplicates match across selected fields. Business duplicates represent the same real entity or event despite differing values, formatting, timestamps, or identifiers. Business deduplication requires a defined key or matching rules, precedence, and auditability.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: Should outliers be removed automatically?
questions.preferred_answer: No. An outlier may be an error, rare valid event, process change, or valuable signal. Validate units and source, examine context and influence, use robust summaries where appropriate, and document any exclusion rule before drawing conclusions.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is a data validity rule?
questions.preferred_answer: It tests whether a value conforms to an allowed domain, format, range, relationship, or business condition, such as end date not preceding start date. Passing validity does not prove real-world accuracy.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is referential integrity, and how would you test it analytically?
questions.preferred_answer: A foreign key should reference an existing permitted parent key unless null is valid. Test unmatched child keys with an anti-join, quantify the affected rows and measures, inspect timing or slowly changing logic, and agree remediation or quarantine.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: How would you reconcile a dashboard total to a source system?
questions.preferred_answer: Align definition, grain, filters, timezone, currency, status, and as-of time. Compare row counts and control totals at progressively finer levels, identify the first divergence, trace transformations, and record tolerances and unresolved timing differences.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: Differentiate data freshness, pipeline latency, and report refresh time.
questions.preferred_answer: Freshness is how current the available data is relative to the real event. Pipeline latency is time from event or source availability to the analytical store. Report refresh time is when the semantic model or visual updates; each can fail independently.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: How should an analytics pipeline respond to unexpected schema drift?
questions.preferred_answer: Detect the change, classify compatible versus breaking, stop or quarantine unsafe data, alert owners, preserve evidence, assess downstream impact, and update contracts, transformations, tests, and documentation through controlled deployment.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is data lineage, and what questions should it answer?
questions.preferred_answer: Lineage shows where data originated, how it was transformed, and which assets consume it. It should help identify owners, code and version, dependencies, quality checks, refresh history, and the downstream impact of a source or definition change.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: How do you set a data-quality threshold?
questions.preferred_answer: Tie it to the decision and harm rather than choosing a convenient percentage. Use historical performance, contractual or regulatory needs, process capability, materiality, segment risk, and remediation cost; specify warning and failure actions.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: When is manual sampling useful in data-quality validation?
questions.preferred_answer: Sampling is useful for checking semantic accuracy against documents or source screens when full automated validation is impractical. Define the population, sampling method, size, reviewer instructions, evidence, disagreement handling, and limits of inference.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What makes a data-cleaning process auditable?
questions.preferred_answer: Keep raw data immutable, implement explicit versioned transformations, log row and value impacts, preserve rejected records and reason codes, test rules, record approvals, and produce before-and-after quality summaries.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: What should a production data-quality monitor include?
questions.preferred_answer: Monitor volume, freshness, schema, key integrity, nulls, distributions, business-rule failures, and critical reconciliations by meaningful segment. Add ownership, severity, suppression rules, run history, escalation, and a link to lineage and recovery instructions.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.category: Data Quality, Profiling, Cleaning, and Reconciliation
questions.question: A null-rate alert fires. How do you investigate without stopping at the symptom?
questions.preferred_answer: Confirm alert validity and scope, compare by source and time, inspect recent code and upstream changes, trace lineage, sample affected records, distinguish delayed from permanently missing data, quantify business impact, fix the generating process, backfill safely, and add a preventive control.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why use an Excel Table instead of an unstructured range?
questions.preferred_answer: Tables expand with data, provide structured references, consistent formulas, filters, totals, and better PivotTable or Power Query inputs. They reduce fragile fixed-range references, though governance and validation are still needed.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How does XLOOKUP improve on common VLOOKUP usage?
questions.preferred_answer: XLOOKUP can return from either direction, uses separate lookup and return arrays, supports an explicit not-found result and match modes, and does not depend on a hard-coded column index. Exact matching should normally be specified intentionally.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: An XLOOKUP returns the wrong business result even though the formula has no error. What might be wrong?
questions.preferred_answer: The key may not be unique, types or spaces may differ, approximate matching may be unintended, the first match may not be the correct effective record, or the lookup table may have stale or duplicated rows. Validate cardinality and business rules, not only formula syntax.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is a PivotTable best suited for?
questions.preferred_answer: It quickly groups, filters, and aggregates tabular data across dimensions for exploration and summarisation. The source must have a consistent header row and appropriate grain; refresh, aggregation type, distinct counts, and calculated logic should be checked.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why can averaging row-level percentages in a spreadsheet be wrong?
questions.preferred_answer: Rows may have different denominators. The correct aggregate rate is often total numerator divided by total denominator, a weighted result. Define the intended grain and calculation rather than averaging pre-calculated percentages blindly.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: When should Power Query be preferred over repeated manual spreadsheet steps?
questions.preferred_answer: Use it for repeatable import, typing, filtering, joining, reshaping, and cleaning. Steps are recorded and refreshable, improving consistency and auditability compared with copy-paste, while still requiring source and error controls.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How would you audit a critical spreadsheet model?
questions.preferred_answer: Map inputs, calculations, and outputs; identify constants and external links; test formula consistency; inspect named ranges; reconcile control totals; challenge assumptions; test edge cases; protect approved cells; and obtain independent review proportional to risk.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Explain relative, absolute, and mixed cell references.
questions.preferred_answer: A relative reference changes by row and column when copied, an absolute reference fixes both with dollar signs, and a mixed reference fixes only row or column. The correct choice depends on the intended replication pattern.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why can dates and times cause spreadsheet errors?
questions.preferred_answer: Dates are stored as serial values and times as fractions, while text that looks like a date may not be numeric. Locale parsing, the 1900 date system, timezone loss, daylight-saving changes, and hidden time components can produce incorrect grouping or comparisons.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What risk should be considered when using dynamic-array formulas?
questions.preferred_answer: Spilled results can change size as data changes and may be blocked by existing cells, tables, or merged cells. Downstream references should deliberately use the spill range and include checks for unexpected size or errors.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How does data validation improve spreadsheet quality, and what does it not guarantee?
questions.preferred_answer: It constrains or warns on entered values using lists, ranges, dates, or custom rules. It reduces input mistakes but may be bypassed by pasting or external processes and does not prove factual accuracy.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How should conditional formatting be used in an analytical workbook?
questions.preferred_answer: Use it to highlight defined exceptions, thresholds, duplicates, or changes, with a clear legend and accessible alternatives. Avoid decorative colour scales that imply unsupported precision or hide values from colour-blind users.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why are external workbook links risky?
questions.preferred_answer: They can break when files move, use stale cached values, hide dependencies, create access problems, and make refresh or review non-reproducible. Prefer governed sources or Power Query and document unavoidable links.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What commonly causes slow Excel workbooks?
questions.preferred_answer: Large used ranges, volatile functions, whole-column array calculations, excessive conditional formatting, repeated lookups, external links, complex dependencies, and unnecessary recalculation. Measure first, reduce calculation scope, and move repeatable transformation to suitable tools.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Why can wrapping every formula in IFERROR be dangerous?
questions.preferred_answer: It may hide genuine logic, reference, or data-quality failures and replace them with plausible blanks or zeros. Handle expected conditions explicitly, retain diagnostics, and distinguish not-found from calculation failure.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What should be included when handing over a business-critical spreadsheet?
questions.preferred_answer: Purpose, owner, source and refresh process, input locations, definitions, assumptions, controls, protected areas, dependencies, known limitations, test evidence, version history, recovery copy, and a simple operating guide.
questions.source_title: UK Government Data Quality Framework Guidance
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the typical logical processing order of a SELECT query?
questions.preferred_answer: Conceptually, FROM and JOIN establish rows, WHERE filters rows, GROUP BY forms groups, HAVING filters groups, SELECT calculates output expressions, DISTINCT removes duplicates, ORDER BY sorts, and LIMIT or FETCH restricts output. Actual optimizers may execute differently.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
questions.preferred_answer: WHERE filters input rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Conditions that can be applied before aggregation are generally clearer and more efficient in WHERE.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Explain INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN.
questions.preferred_answer: INNER returns matched combinations; LEFT preserves every left row plus matches; RIGHT preserves every right row; FULL preserves rows from both sides and fills unmatched columns with nulls. Join conditions and cardinality determine row multiplication.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How does NULL behave in SQL comparisons?
questions.preferred_answer: NULL represents unknown or absent, so ordinary comparisons produce unknown rather than true. Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL, understand three-valued logic, and treat COALESCE as a business decision rather than automatic cleanup.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How would you calculate total revenue by month and region?
questions.preferred_answer: Select a consistent month expression and region, sum the governed revenue measure, filter the intended population, group by month and region, and order explicitly. State timezone, currency, status, and whether returns or tax are included.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: Differentiate COUNT(*), COUNT(column), and COUNT(DISTINCT column).
questions.preferred_answer: COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT(column) counts non-null values in that expression, and COUNT(DISTINCT column) counts distinct non-null values. None automatically means unique business entities unless the column represents one.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is CASE used for in SQL?
questions.preferred_answer: CASE expresses conditional logic for labels, bucketing, conditional aggregation, or ordering. Categories should be mutually understood, edge cases handled, and an ELSE branch used deliberately to expose or classify unexpected values.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What does COALESCE do, and what is a common misuse?
questions.preferred_answer: It returns the first non-null expression. A misuse is replacing unknown values with zero or text without confirming that the substitution is semantically valid, which can distort averages and reconciliation.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL?
questions.preferred_answer: UNION combines compatible result sets and removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL retains all rows and is usually cheaper. Choose based on business meaning, not as a shortcut to hide duplicated data.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: When would you use a common table expression rather than a nested subquery?
questions.preferred_answer: A CTE can name logical steps, improve readability, support recursion, and allow a complex query to be reasoned about in stages. It does not automatically improve performance; optimizer behaviour and reuse should be checked.
questions.integrity_note: Original MapIT preparation question; not an employer assessment leak.

questions.question: How do you find customers with no orders?
questions.preferred_answer: Use NOT EXISTS with a correlated condition or a LEFT JOIN followed by a null check on a non-null order key. NOT EXISTS is often clear and avoids the NULL pitfalls of NOT IN.

questions.question: How does clustering complement partitioning?

questions.question: Why is columnar storage effective for analytics?

questions.question: What is a shuffle in distributed data processing, and why is it expensive?
questions.preferred_answer: A shuffle redistributes data across workers for joins, groupings, or sorts, requiring network transfer, serialization, memory and disk. Reduce unnecessary shuffles with partition-aware design, early filtering, suitable joins, and balanced keys.

questions.question: How does data skew affect a distributed analytics job?

questions.question: Why are many small files problematic in a data lake?

questions.question: When is a broadcast join useful?

Check expected partitions, source availability, filters, watermarks, rejected rows, joins, and write mode; compare counts and control totals; block downstream publication, correct and idempotently rerun, reconcile, and add volume and completeness controls.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Communicate the distinction between run status and data status, impacted products, safe-use guidance, root cause, recovery evidence and prevention.

practical_scenarios.title: Tableau trend is visually misleading
practical_scenarios.situation: A dashboard uses a dual axis with different scales, making customer satisfaction appear to track revenue closely.
practical_scenarios.candidate_task: Explain how you would review and redesign it.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Check the analytical claim and correlation, inspect scales and time alignment, remove the visual implication by using aligned small multiples, a shared indexed view, or a properly labelled relationship plot, and include uncertainty and relevant events. Do not imply causation.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Explain the visual risk to the author and owner, propose a corrected view, and identify any decisions or external communications that used the misleading chart.
practical_scenarios.source_title: Tableau Help - Which chart or graph is right for you?
practical_scenarios.integrity_note: Original MapIT scenario; not a leaked employer case.

practical_scenarios.title: Cloud query costs triple
practical_scenarios.situation: Monthly BigQuery cost triples although dashboard usage is stable.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Attribute cost by project, user, query and table; compare bytes scanned, partitions, clustering, scheduled jobs, retries, extracts and new views; look for missing partition filters, full refreshes, cross joins or repeated queries. Optimise the highest verified drivers and add budgets, guardrails and cost ownership.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Report cost impact, confirmed drivers, immediate containment, trade-offs of proposed changes, owner and expected savings without claiming savings before measurement.
practical_scenarios.integrity_note: Original MapIT scenario; not a leaked employer case.

practical_scenarios.title: Correlation is presented as a driver
practical_scenarios.situation: An analysis finds that high app usage is associated with retention and recommends forcing more notifications to increase usage.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Usage may be a consequence of satisfaction or share confounders with retention. Define the intervention, examine timing and segments, control for plausible confounders, consider randomised notification tests, and add guardrails for opt-outs, annoyance and trust. The observational association does not justify the causal action.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Reframe the finding as an association, state what evidence would support causality, and flag customer-harm and privacy considerations before experimentation.
practical_scenarios.integrity_note: Original MapIT scenario; not a leaked employer case.

practical_scenarios.title: External partner requests raw customer data
practical_scenarios.situation: A partner says raw customer events are needed to improve a joint campaign and asks for a CSV by email.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Clarify purpose and necessity, authority and contract, fields and recipients, data classification, retention, location and security, then seek accountable privacy, legal and data-owner approval. Minimise or aggregate data, use an approved secure transfer, log access, set deletion terms and verify compliance.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Do not send the file while review is pending. Record the request, risk, decision owner, approved alternative and any deadline impact.
practical_scenarios.integrity_note: Original MapIT scenario; not a leaked employer case.

practical_scenarios.title: Timestamp migration shifts daily totals
practical_scenarios.situation: After moving from an on-premise database to a cloud warehouse, orders near midnight appear on different business dates.
practical_scenarios.candidate_task: Explain the likely issue and remediation.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Identify whether timestamps were naive, local or UTC, compare source and target types and conversion rules, account for daylight-saving transitions, define the business timezone and event date, correct transformation logic, backfill affected periods, and reconcile by instant and local date.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: State affected dates and metrics, whether historical reports change, the approved timezone definition, correction plan and consumer guidance.
practical_scenarios.integrity_note: Original MapIT scenario; not a leaked employer case.

practical_scenarios.title: Dashboard is popular but no decision improves
practical_scenarios.situation: A dashboard has high page views, but operational teams still export data and make decisions in separate spreadsheets.
practical_scenarios.candidate_task: Explain how you would assess and improve the product.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Observe user tasks, identify trust, definition, latency, granularity, workflow, access or usability gaps, measure decision time and manual work rather than views, prioritise a minimum workflow improvement, retire redundant elements, and validate outcomes with users after release.
practical_scenarios.escalation_communication: Share findings without blaming users; distinguish adoption from value, name product and process owners, and agree measurable success and a review date.
